Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Mateo has been asking to continue after his school music club ended, and he has been practicing on our upright piano at home most evenings. He can read basic music and knows the names of the keys, but he is still a beginner and has not had private lessons before. I don’t want to make it sound like he has more experience than he does.

Luis, my husband, checked our family calendar last night and suggested Tuesday afternoons because he can drive Mateo then. He said, “Tuesday is the one day I can reliably get away from work before five.” I checked the school schedule too, and Mateo is out at 3:10, so a 4:30 start should leave enough time to get across town without having to rush straight from the school door. We live near the north library, and the studio is on Alder Street, so the drive is usually about twenty minutes when traffic is normal. On rainy days it can take longer, which is another reason I’d rather not ask for a lesson that begins right at four.

The time I’m asking for is Tuesday at 4:30 with Jo, for a 45-minute lesson each week, beginning October 15. If Jo has that weekly time available, please book Mateo for it. If it isn’t available, please check with me before booking a different time or putting him on a waitlist. I can sometimes make Wednesdays work, but that depends on Luis’s work schedule, and I don’t want to say yes to a Wednesday slot until I’ve checked with him. We are not asking for a trial lesson with a different teacher; Mateo would like to work with Jo because he heard her play at the studio’s spring student concert.

There are a few details that may help with the booking. Mateo’s full name is Mateo Ruiz, and his birthday is February 8, 2013. My best contact number is the one already on the family account, ending in 4826; email is also fine for schedule questions. If the studio needs a separate emergency contact, use Luis Ruiz at the number ending in 9173. Please list me as the parent who requested the lesson, even though Luis may be the one who brings Mateo on Tuesdays. If a form asks who will usually attend, the answer is Mateo, with either parent dropping him off and picking him up.

1. We can bring a notebook, pencil, and the beginner piano book Mateo already has, if Jo is happy to use it. The book is called First Steps at the Piano, by Nora Bell, and it is the blue edition. I’m not asking the studio to order another copy. Mateo’s school teacher recommended that he keep a practice log, so we can bring that too, though it is only a sheet in a folder and not a formal book.
2. Our piano at home is an upright with 88 keys, and it is tuned, although the low A has started to sound a little dull. Mateo can practice there, but he does not have a keyboard to bring to lessons. I’m mentioning the low note in case Jo asks what kind of instrument he uses; it is not a request for the studio to arrange a repair or assess the piano.
3. We have read the studio’s usual cancellation note. If Mateo is ill, I’ll contact the studio as soon as I can rather than bring him in. I understand that the studio may have its own notice period, but I couldn’t tell from the page whether a missed lesson can be made up. Please send me the current policy or point me to the right page; I’m not asking you to promise a makeup lesson.
4. Luis asked whether the first payment is due when the lesson is booked or at the first visit. I don’t know which way the studio handles it, so please let me know the amount and due date once you confirm the schedule. We can pay by card or check, and I don’t need you to charge anything before we know which time is available.

One calendar complication is that Mateo’s school is closed for fall break on Tuesday, October 22. If Jo’s Tuesday time is available and the booking starts on October 15, please leave October 22 out and have the next lesson be October 29; we will be out of town that week and cannot attend remotely. I don’t want that week moved to Wednesday or counted as a request for an extra lesson. If the regular weekly start would instead be later than October 15, let me know what date you have in mind before applying the fall-break note, because the October 22 detail only matters if Mateo is already scheduled to begin before then.

Jo told Mateo after the spring concert, “We can start with short pieces and build up from there,” and he came home excited about choosing music with her. I’m not expecting him to learn a particular song right away, and I haven’t promised him a performance date. He does enjoy film music and simple tunes he can recognize, so that may be useful background for Jo, but I’d rather let her decide what is appropriate for a first lesson. Could you pass that along when you send her the booking request? If she needs any more information about his playing level or the book, I can answer by email.
